content: Assunta Hospital, also known as Hospital Assunta in Malay, is a renowned private healthcare institution located in Petaling Jaya, Selangor, Malaysia. It holds the distinction of being the first private hospital established in the area. The hospital was founded in 1957 by the Franciscan Missionaries of Mary (FMM). Its construction was made possible through the generous contributions of the public, the Social Welfare Department, and both local and government grants. In 1961, Assunta Hospital established the first private nursing school in Malaysia, known as the Assunta College of Nursing. This institution has gained a strong reputation for its high-quality nursing education. Graduates of the Assunta College of Nursing are recognized for their professional excellence and compassionate care. Assunta Hospital operates as a charitable organization and is overseen by a Board of Directors. This board includes FMM Sisters, professionals, and business leaders who serve on an honorary basis. Over the years, the hospital has evolved into a modern specialist facility, now equipped with 350 beds and staffed by 700 healthcare professionals. The hospital is particularly noted for its patient-centred approach to care and its exceptional nursing services. In addition to its medical services, Assunta Hospital has a longstanding tradition of providing pastoral care. This includes addressing the physical, psychological, moral, and spiritual needs of its patients. The hospital is equipped to handle a wide range of medical specialities and is committed to staying at the forefront of medical advancements and technology. Its philosophy emphasizes the importance of a professional learning environment for its staff, with a strong focus on continuing education to enhance patient care. One notable individual associated with the hospital is Salmah Ismail, better known as Saloma, the wife and widow of the legendary Malaysian entertainer P. Ramlee. She passed away at Assunta Hospital in 1982. However, the hospital has recently faced criticism due to a controversy involving the refusal to treat a patient, who subsequently passed away a few hours later.
